title: Supreme Court: Opati v. Republic of Sudan
summary: Plaintiffs in a suit against a foreign state for personal injury or death caused by acts of terrorism under 28 U. S. C. §1605A(c) may seek punitive damages for preenactment conduct. (No. 17-1268, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 590 U.S. 418).

title: Supreme Court: Lucky Brand Dungarees, Inc. v. Marcel Fashions Group, Inc.
summary: Because the trademark action at issue challenged different conduct—and raised different claims—from an earlier action between the parties, Marcel cannot preclude Lucky Brand from raising new defenses, including a defense that Lucky Brand failed to press fully in the earlier suit. (No. 18-1086, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 590 U.S. 405).

title: Supreme Court: Kelly v. United States
summary: Because the scheme to reduce the number of George Washington Bridge toll lanes dedicated to Fort Lee, New Jersey, morning commuters as political retribution against Fort Lee’s mayor did not aim to obtain money or property from the federal Port Authority, Baroni and Kelly could not have violated the federal-program fraud or wire fraud laws. (No. 18-1059, opinion by Justice Kagan; 590 U.S. 391).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Sineneng-Smith
summary: The Ninth Circuit panel’s drastic departure from the principle of party presentation constituted an abuse of discretion where the court reached out to decide a question never raised by respondent, namely, whether 8 U. S. C. §1324(a)(1)(A)(iv) is unconstitutionally overbroad. (No. 19-67, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 590 U.S. 371).
